messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED: Spike in KMS signing errors observed across multiple regions (us-west1, europe-west2). Auto-page issued to oncall.

sam (oncall): saw the alert. Are startups failing or only live signing? Pulling up dashboards.

neha (eng-run): both. New node init sequences that call KMS Sign are timing out causing crashloops. Also on-path request signing has elevated 5xx.

tom (eng-runtime): stack traces show requests stuck in kms_client.Sign with context deadlines and retries stacking up: ```
ERROR runtime/sign.go:87 sign failed: context deadline exceeded
WARN runtime/retry.go:44 retry loop launched, backoff=2s
```

lisa (support): support queue: 8 customers reported deploy failures; a few dedicated customers see session creation 502s. CSMs alerted.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do without provider help?

neha (eng-run): plan: 1) enable ephemeral local signing cache (fallback) to allow startups 2) enable async-sign queue for non-blocking startup 3) route service signing to secondary KMS region (if configured) 4) open provider tickets.

paul (ops): I'm toggling the ephemeral cache flag in env store: `KMS_FALLBACK=ephemeral_cache` and `KMS_CACHE_MAX_AGE=1h`. Doing a canary on staging first.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/runtime-service: rev=2007 -> canary-nodes(us-east1-3).

sam (oncall): canary logs?

tom (eng-runtime): canary succeeded. Startup no longer waits on KMS. Async-sign queue draining in background. Logs: ```
INFO runtime/startup.go: node boot ok, keys: served_from_cache
INFO sign/queue.go: enqueued async-sign job id=abc123
```

neha (eng-run): opened AWS case: 89211 and GCP case: 90012 — both indicating elevated KMS API latency in the impacted zones. Linking both to ticketing.

sam (oncall): good. Let's push config to critical clusters with a phased rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and a safety rollback if error rate > 3% in 5m.

lisa (support): communicating to affected customers: "We're applying a temporary fallback to cached/ephemeral signing to restore service while cloud KMS recovers. No action required on your side." Sent template to CSMs.

neha (eng-run): note on safety: ephemeral cache uses short TTL and signs with cached public keys only for session bootstrap. We must not rely on it for long-running session rotation. Setting `KMS_CACHE_MAX_AGE=1h` and `KMS_EPHEMERAL=true`.

paul (ops): rolling to critical clusters now. Monitoring dashboards: requests/sec and sign-error-rate streaming.

sam (oncall): vendor status?

neha (eng-run): GCP status page reporting "KMS API degraded in europe-west2" link: https://status.cloud.google.com/incident/kms/90012. AWS status shows partial elevated latency in regions tied to our accounts: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/89211. Both teams engaged.

infra-bot: Alerting: escalate to infra-lead if error rate stays above 4% for >10m.

sam (oncall): temporary mitigation metrics: sign error rate dropped from 7.1% -> 1.0% within 8 minutes after canary. Latency improved for start paths. 

tom (eng-runtime): found a retry loop bug where exponential backoff doubled beyond 60s causing worker accumulation under KMS slowness. Adding backpressure and max-retry cap (now 6 retries, cap 30s). Filing BUG-4510.

neha (eng-run): provider update: GCP applied a routing patch; they report partial recovery and continue monitoring. AWS reports they're throttling high-volume control-plane requests; mitigation in progress.

lisa (support): collecting logs for post-incident summary: grep pattern `kms_sign` across last 24h, uploaded to secure share. Shared with enterprise CSMs and affected accounts.

sam (oncall): handoff plan: I'll remain on thread for 30 more minutes then pass to night oncall if stable. Please document all temporary flags and owners.

paul (ops): oncall accept for handoff. I'll run a 30m cadence and escalate if sign error rate >2.5%.

infra-bot: Handoff recorded: incident 2182223333 owner sam -> paul.

sam (oncall): commands used during mitigation: ```bash
# flip ephemeral cache in env store
vault kv put secret/runtime KMS_FALLBACK=ephemeral_cache KMS_EPHEMERAL=true KMS_CACHE_MAX_AGE=1h
# k8s restart rollout
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/runtime-service
# quick health check
curl -sS https://runtime.internal/health | jq .kms_sign_status
```

tom (eng-runtime): post-incident followups: - add a fail-fast timeout for sign RPCs (3s) - surface cache-hit metrics and stale-key alarms - add an automated multi-provider fallback test to CI - reduce retry amplification and add circuit breaker.

neha (eng-run): owners: tom -> runtime fixes, neha -> rollout automation + alerts, paul -> runbook + paging thresholds, lisa -> customer comms. Creating postmortem doc and scheduling blameless review.

incident-bot: Incident 2182223333 status: mitigated (temporary fallback enabled). Duration so far: ~9m since detection.

lisa (support): update sent to customers summarizing mitigation and next steps; promised follow-up after root cause.

paul (ops): monitoring stable at 0.9% sign error rate for 15m. Keeping thread open for 1 hour then archiving.

sam (oncall): thanks team. Leave any remaining notes in the postmortem doc. Remember to test the multi-kms fallback in staging so we can avoid vendor single points of failure.
